heroHeadline: Al Arabiya Leaks 'Final Draft' US-Iran Deal — Could Be Announced 'Within Hours'; House GOP Pulls War Powers Vote; Trump: Hormuz Must Be 'Open and Free'; Day 84
heroSubtitle: Day 84 (May 22): Saudi broadcaster Al Arabiya published what it described as the 'final draft' of a comprehensive US-Iran peace framework, citing a source saying the deal could be announced 'within hours.' The leaked terms include an immediate ceasefire on all fronts, freedom of Hormuz navigation, gradual sanctions relief, a joint monitoring mechanism, and nuclear negotiations to begin within 7 days — with the enrichment moratorium duration deferred to post-deal talks. Oil markets fell ~5% to ~$103/bbl and US equities surged ~$500B on the news. However, neither Washington nor Tehran confirmed the deal by end of day, and Pakistan Army Chief Munir's planned Tehran trip was called off because the 'final formula' was not yet in place — Interior Minister Naqvi traveled instead. Trump explicitly demanded the Strait of Hormuz be 'open and free' with no Iranian tolls. House Republican leaders pulled an Iran War Powers Resolution vote after it appeared to have enough bipartisan support to pass — the first WPR vote to be pulled rather than voted down, delayed to June. Secretary Rubio cited 'good signs' and 'slight progress' but cautioned against premature optimism.
